relations: Shallow water advancing and receding across the foreground pebbles shifts which rocks appear glossy and wet.
Ripples on the open water surface cause the sun's reflection to break into moving bright highlights.
The stationary glass sphere's refracted light streak flickers faintly in response to the external water motion.
The tide washes around the base of the sphere while the sphere and horizon remain steady.
caption:
The video captures a transparent glass sphere resting on a wet, dark pebble shore in the left foreground. Its curved surface refracts an inverted image of the low sun and the distant horizon. To the right, the sun hangs just above a thin strip of land on calm water, casting a vertical column of shimmering light beneath an orange-pink sky. The framing stays fixed, and the sphere holds its position on the stones throughout.

Already underway when the clip opens, shallow water laps in and out across the foreground pebbles. The waterline advances to cover more stones and then recedes to expose them again, shifting which rocks appear glossy and wet. The sun's reflection on the open water breaks apart into moving bright highlights as the surface ripples, and the refracted streak inside the sphere flickers faintly with this external motion. The horizon and the sun itself remain steady, so the visible activity is confined to the gentle, repeating wash of the tide around the stationary ball.
